extraction.input_text: On the issue of whether Henry committed insider trading, Alice's statement to Bob that Henry told her he had a "great tip about what a certain stock was going to do."

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: Alice made a statement to Bob outside of the current trial or hearing context.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be made by the declarant while not testifying at the current trial or hearing.

arguments.text: The statement asserts that Henry told Alice he had a "great tip about what a certain stock was going to do," constituting a factual assertion.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be one that the declarant asserts.
arguments.evidence_span: that Henry told her he had a "great tip about what a certain stock was going to do."

arguments.text: The statement is introduced on the issue of whether Henry committed insider trading, indicating it is offered to prove the truth of Henry's alleged tip.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) defines hearsay as a statement offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Henry committed insider trading, Alice's statement to Bob that Henry told her...

arguments.text: There is no indication the statement is offered for a non-hearsay purpose such as notice, effect on listener, or impeachment.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) hearsay analysis requires confirming the statement is not offered for a non-hearsay purpose.

arguments.text: If Henry is a party to the case, his statement might be admissible as a party-opponent admission under FRE 801(d)(2), which would treat it as non-hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(d)(2) excludes party-opponent admissions from the definition of hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of whether Henry committed insider trading
